title: The day after
hookLine: as the Prophet ﷺ is prepared for burial, the Ansar and the Muhajirun meet at the portico of Banu Sa'idah

cards: In a small room beside the mosque in Medina, the body of the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, lies still. His family are with him. Outside, the city is in shock.

And a short walk away, under a roofed shelter that belongs to a clan called Banu Sa'idah, men of the Ansar are gathering. They have a question no one in this community has ever had to answer. He is gone.
Who leads us now? Today: the day after.

teach.b: Sahih al-Bukhari, in a report from Aisha, gives us the hours. When the news spreads, Umar ibn al-Khattab stands up and insists the Prophet has not died.
Then Abu Bakr arrives from outside the city. He uncovers the Prophet's face, kisses him, and says that God will not make him taste death twice. He comes out and speaks to the crowd.

Whoever worshipped Muhammad, Muhammad has died. Whoever worships God, God is living and does not die. Then he recites a verse of Surah Al Imran: Muhammad is only a messenger, and messengers passed away before him.
If he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels? Ibn Abbas, in a report Bukhari places alongside hers, says it was as if people had never heard the verse until that moment.

teach.h: THE ANSAR GATHER AT THE SAQIFAH.
teach.b: Meanwhile the Ansar, the people of Medina who had taken the Prophet in, gather at the saqifah of Banu Sa'idah, the roofed portico, around Sa'd ibn Ubadah.

teach.h: A LEADER FROM US, AND FROM YOU.
teach.b: Their first proposal, in Bukhari's report: a leader from us, and a leader from you, the Muhajirun who came from Mecca. Word reaches Abu Bakr and Umar, and they go, with Abu Ubaydah.
What happens there, and what it means, is where Muslims' memories divide. Sunni Muslims tell it one way, and tomorrow is theirs. Shia Muslims tell it another, and the day after belongs to them.
Today, stay with the hour before any answer: a community that has lost the one who received revelation, grief and fear and duty in the air at once, and everyone asking the same two words.

how: Muslims remember the Prophet's death through the reports of that day, and Abu Bakr's words, that God is living and does not die, are quoted at times of loss.

Sunni and Shia Muslims tell it differently. the next two days set out each telling.

games.q: you're one of the Ansar. the Prophet has just died, and Medina is in shock. what do you do?
o: gather at the saqifah and propose a leader from each side.
games.why: Bukhari reports the Ansar gathered with Sa'd ibn Ubadah and proposed: a leader from us, and a leader from you.

practice: Remember a time someone who held things together was suddenly gone: a parent, a coach, a boss, a teacher.

Notice the shock, and the practical questions arriving before the grief had room, and let both be true: the loss, and the need to go on. If you pray, you can pray for those who lead your community, and for those who grieve.

wordCard.voice: Saqifah. The roofed shelter where the Ansar met, the day the Prophet died, to ask who would lead, while his family stayed with his body. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: a roofed shelter or portico; the saqifah of Banu Sa'idah.

carryVoice: Your line: what now? Before any answer, there was a loss to name. Until tomorrow.
